messages:
mira: Heads-up — after the 03:10 rollout of the streaming-proxy header change we're seeing a big uptick in 502/503s from the hosted API. Canary was supposed to be 10% but errors jump started ~03:15. :fire:
ops-bot: deploy-notify: Deployment streaming-proxy-v2 started at 03:09 UTC, roll percentage=10%
alex_oncall: I see the spike on the gateway graph, 502s up ~6x across regions. Tail logs show a lot of upstream RST/timeouts to auth-backend.
jordan_eng: Did the canary config include the new opaque header rename? I thought we gated with the flag enable-new-proxy-headers=false by default.
support_jenny: We're getting multiple customer tickets reporting "API returning 503s" and timeouts while uploading large prompt payloads. Customers are in EU and NA.
sam_sre: Quick check: routing service report shows one of the traffic-slice selectors accidentally mapped 30% -> streaming-proxy-v2 due to a missing env in the rollout job. That would explain rate of hits. Confirming logs now.
mira: yikes — that explains it. Can we throttle/stop the rollout?
jordan_eng: Pushing stop now. /rollout pause streaming-proxy-v2 (cmd run)
ops-bot: rollout-update: streaming-proxy-v2 paused at 03:20 UTC, current traffic 29%
sam_sre: Repro steps from a dev box: curl -v -H "X-Streaming-Proxy: new-opaque" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/gen\" --data-binary @payload.json
sam_sre: Stack excerpt:
```
2024-08-12T03:14:23Z gateway warn upstream timeout waiting for auth-backend
2024-08-12T03:14:23Z auth-client ERR 401 malformed header: expected 'x-rw-auth' got 'x-stream-opaque'
2024-08-12T03:14:23Z gateway ERROR returning 502 to client
```
jordan_eng: Looks like auth-backend treats the renamed header as unknown and fails fast, but when the proxy retries we hit connection churn and timeouts. Two issues: header rename and the selector misconfiguration.
sarah_cs: We're coordinating with affected customers; CS requests ETA for rollback and confirmation when stable.
alex_oncall: Plan: 1) rollback flag to previous mapping (set enable-new-proxy-headers=false at global scope) 2) revert traffic-slice to 10% 3) verify 5xx trend return to baseline 4) follow-up postmortem. I'm executing step 1 now.
jordan_eng: Rolling flag rollback: /config set enable-new-proxy-headers=false --scope global --who jordan_eng (cmd run)
ops-bot: config-update: enable-new-proxy-headers set to false at 03:25 UTC by jordan_eng
sam_sre: Reverting traffic-slice now to 10% (cmd run)
ops-bot: rollout-update: streaming-proxy-v2 traffic set to 10% at 03:27 UTC
alex_oncall: Charts: 502/503s dropping back toward baseline within 4 minutes of traffic revert. Still monitoring for residual auth rejections.
support_jenny: Notified customers that we rolled back and are monitoring — will update ticket threads. :thumbsup:
mira: thanks team. We'll keep this thread for follow-up. Next actions: postmortem + fix rollout job to enforce env for targeting and add a guard to reject header renames without a canary flag.
